title: Git branches and merging
body: A Git branch is a movable pointer to a commit; creating one writes a single 41-byte file, which is why branching is effectively free. The branch you are on is tracked by HEAD. Merging combines histories: a fast-forward merge simply moves the branch pointer when the target is a direct descendant, while a three-way merge creates a new merge commit with two parents using the common ancestor as the base. Rebasing replays commits on top of another branch, producing a linear history but rewriting commit hashes — which is why you should never rebase commits that others have already pulled.
